items_missed: Section 1 (Set Agenda): transcript opens straight into signal-issue small talk and the condo unit number — no name check-in, no 'how are you today,' no recap of details on file, no move-date availability check, no agenda statement, no explicit 'sound good?' close.

Section 2 (Probe): never asked for a full street address/zip at either origin building or the destination condo, never asked about packing service needs, never asked the 'anything you're particularly worried about with this move' stressor question.

Section 3 (Pricing): no 'pricing is super simple' opener, no rundown of what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools), No Worries Damage Coverage came up only as a TV-cord exclusion — never explained as the actual $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover never mentioned, On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, no full 'no hidden fees' pitch.
Section 4 (Clock): never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never did a sense-check ('does that make sense?') after walking through the minimum and proration.

Section 5 (Estimate): no equivalents/analogy used to make the 5.5-hour estimate tangible (e.g., a size comparison) — everything else about the buildup (stairs, walk distance, disassembly, movers/truck count) was covered.
Section 6 (Save Your Ass): skipped entirely — no mention that prep shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no close.

Section 7 (Quote/Booking): explicitly said 'no pressure for that now' instead of attempting to book today, never mentioned a bolded summary at the top of the confirmation email, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' before cutting the call short for another call, never gave office hours or how to reach the team.
Section 8 (Politeness): used the customer's name only once, at the very end, and got it wrong ('miss Autum') — short of the 3+ target.
Section 9 (Bonus): No Worries coverage was only explained as a TV exclusion, with no mention of the $2,000 cap or the 60 cents/lb baseline liability valuation.
top_strength: Hector ran an unusually complex two-origin move (two separate apartments consolidating into one condo) with real patience and thoroughness — he asked about stairs, parking, TV mounting, and exterior storage separately for both units without losing the thread, then built the 5.5-hour estimate transparently in front of the customer: "So all in all for your move estimate, I do have that set for at about five and a half hours," showing his math (load time per unit plus unload) rather than just handing her a number.
coaching_note: Your detail-gathering on a genuinely tricky two-address move was excellent, but you skipped the two moments that matter most: there's no agenda opener up front and no Save Your Ass prep speech anywhere in the call — on a move this size, prep tips are the easiest lever you have to shrink her bill. You also undercut your own close by telling her 'no pressure for that now' instead of attempting to book, and you ended the call abruptly for another line without asking if she had more questions or using her name. Tighten the open and the close — the middle of this call is strong.
phone_presence_notes: Consistent affirmations ("Awesome," "Nice," "gotcha") and a light, natural moment of rapport about buying new furniture kept the customer comfortable and positive through a long, detail-heavy call, though the rushed goodbye keeps it from a 5.
